root_cause.text: The driver unnecessarily transmitted garbage data during emulated read-only dual/quad SPI transfers, corrupting the bus because QSPI lacks a dedicated master-out line and the hardware core already generates the required clock cycles for reads.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "The core will deal with reads by creating clock cycles itself, there's no need to generate clock cycles by transmitting garbage data at the driver level…transmitting garbage data just bricks the transfer since QSPI doesn't have a dedicated master-out line like MOSI in regular SPI." The patch modifies the transfer logic to call `mchp_coreqspi_read_op()` instead of `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()` when `dual_quad` is true and no `tx_buf` is present, thereby avoiding the harmful transmission.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect handling of dual/quad SPI transfers by routing them to a dedicated read operation instead of the combined write-read operation.
intent_record.what: Added a boolean variable 'dual_quad' to detect when the transfer uses DUAL or QUAD line widths, and modified the conditional logic to call mchp_coreqspi_read_op for such transfers instead of mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op.
intent_record.how: At runtime, transfers with rx_buf and dual/quad mode now use a separate read operation rather than the combined write-read operation, ensuring correct behavior for multi-line SPI transfers.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly address the vulnerability by routing dual/quad SPI transfers to a dedicated read operation, avoiding the transmission of garbage data during emulated read-only transfers.

candidates.rationale: Sets tx_len to the full transfer length even for read-only dual/quad transfers, causing the combined write-read operation to transmit garbage data.
Sets txbuf to the tx_buf pointer, which may be NULL or contain garbage for read-only transfers; used by the combined operation to transmit unwanted data.
Invokes the combined write-read operation for all transfers with a rx_buf, including read-only dual/quad transfers, leading to transmission of garbage data on the bus.
